To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of chemical agents in reverse osmosi desalination process, can cause an environmental impact on coastal ecosystem, and that the use of biocides as C 5 H O 2 in desalination process is not recommended.

the toxicity of the chemical mixtures in reverse osmoses (RO) concentrates is reduced by antagonism, which can be attributed to a reduction in the toxicity of the most toxic compound (C5H8O2) in the mixtures.

the use of chemical compounds in the RO desalination process is a concern for the marine environment, especially in the presence of biocides; the use of binary mixtures of chemical compounds in RO desalination is a concern for marine environment; and the use of binary mixture of chemical compounds in desalination process could be more toxic than single compounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a toxicological assessment of chemical mixtures and individually, used in desalination process, in order to evaluate the environmental impact on the coastal ecosystem.
the development of a methodology for the environmental evaluation of the desalination processes, which can be applied in other areas of the world.

the development of a methodology for the environmental assessment of chemical mixtures used in the RO desalination process, which will contribute to the development of sustainable desalination technologies in coastal zones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the application of the biocide C 5 H8 O 2 is not a viable option to control biofouling in the reverse osmosis membranes, due to its high toxicity and its strong antagonistic effect with other chemical compounds used in desalination.
the use of C 5 H O 2 in the desalination concentrate would be a good alternative for the use of NaClO, CuSO 4, KMnO 3 and FeCl 3 in the same conditions.
the toxicity of chemical mixtures in the RO desalination is a function of the chemical composition of the concentrate and the chemical compounds used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chemical compounds used in desalination process have a high risk on marine environment, but the risk could be reduced significantly with the application of binary mixtures of biocides.
, the use of biocides is a necessary step in the desalination industry to prevent biofouling.
the toxicity of binary mixture is not always additive or synergic, but can be also antagonistic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of biocide C 5 H8O2 in reverse osmosi desalination is not recommended, because the toxicity of this chemical agent in the concentrate is very high.
the use of chemical compounds during the RO desalination process can be done with a minimum risk on the marine environment, since the toxicity observed in the bioassay was low.

the toxicity of the chemicals used during desalination process is not additive and the use of a mixture of these compounds in the desalination concentrate does not represent a significant risk for marine ecosystems.
